items.stem: Which line shows the equation for photosynthesis written in chemical symbols?

options.text: CO2 and H2O react to form C6H12O6 and O2.
C6H12O6 and O2 react to form CO2 and H2O.
CO2 and O2 react to form C6H12O6 and H2O.
CO2 and H2O react to form C6H12O6 and heat.

items.why: This is the equation carbon dioxide + water → (light) glucose + oxygen written with the chemical symbols CO2, H2O, C6H12O6 and O2.

items.stem: Which statement describes photosynthesis as an endothermic reaction?

options.text: Energy is transferred from the chloroplasts to the surroundings.
Energy is transferred from the environment to the chloroplasts.
Energy is transferred from the surroundings to the mitochondria.
Energy is transferred from the glucose to the environment as heat.

items.why: Photosynthesis is an endothermic reaction in which energy is transferred from the environment to the chloroplasts by light.

items.stem: A student measures the rate of photosynthesis of pondweed by counting bubbles of oxygen. She counts 90 bubbles in 3 minutes. What is the rate of photosynthesis?

options.text: 30 bubbles per minute
90 bubbles per minute
270 bubbles per minute
0.03 bubbles per minute

items.why: Rate is the amount of product divided by the time taken: 90 bubbles ÷ 3 minutes = 30 bubbles per minute.

items.stem: A lamp is moved from 10 cm to 20 cm from a piece of pondweed. Light intensity is inversely proportional to the square of the distance from the lamp. What happens to the light intensity reaching the pondweed?

options.text: It falls to 1/2 of the intensity at 10 cm.
It falls to 1/16 of the intensity at 10 cm.
It falls to 1/4 of the intensity at 10 cm.
It falls to 1/20 of the intensity at 10 cm.

items.why: The distance is doubled, so the light intensity falls by a factor of 2 squared: it becomes one quarter of the intensity at 10 cm.

items.stem: How does a plant obtain the amino acids it uses for protein synthesis?

options.text: Amino acids are made from starch and nitrate ions.
Amino acids are made from glucose and nitrate ions.
Amino acids are absorbed from the soil by the roots.
Proteins are absorbed from the soil by the roots.

items.why: Glucose produced in photosynthesis is used to produce amino acids, and to do this plants also use nitrate ions that are absorbed from the soil.

items.stem: A student plots the rate of photosynthesis of pondweed against light intensity at a constant temperature. The graph rises steeply and then becomes a horizontal line. Which statement explains the horizontal part of the graph?

options.text: Light intensity is still limiting the rate on the flat part.
The plant has switched from photosynthesis to respiration.
The rate is still rising but the graph is not showing it.
Another factor, such as temperature, is now limiting the rate.

items.why: The factors interact and any one of them may be the factor that limits photosynthesis. Once light intensity is no longer limiting, temperature or carbon dioxide concentration limits the rate, so the rate stops rising.

items.stem: A graph shows the rate of photosynthesis against light intensity at 20 °C and at 30 °C, both at the same carbon dioxide concentration. Both curves rise and then become horizontal, but the 30 °C curve becomes horizontal at a higher rate. Which statement about the graph is correct?

options.text: Light intensity is limiting the rate where the 20 °C curve is flat.
Temperature is limiting the rate on the steep part of each curve.
Temperature is limiting the rate where the 20 °C curve is flat.
Raising the temperature to 50 °C would raise the flat part again.

items.why: On the flat part, increasing light intensity has no effect, but raising the temperature to 30 °C gives a higher rate. The factor that raises the rate when it alone is increased is the limiting factor.

items.stem: Which statement describes cellular respiration?

options.text: an endothermic reaction happening in all living cells
an exothermic reaction happening during hard exercise
an exothermic reaction happening in all living cells
an exothermic reaction happening when we breathe in

items.why: Cellular respiration is an exothermic reaction which is continuously occurring in living cells, transferring the energy needed for living processes.

items.stem: Which is a use of the energy transferred by respiration?

options.text: creating new energy inside the living cell
moving oxygen from the lungs to the blood
building larger molecules from smaller ones
breaking large molecules into smaller ones

items.why: Organisms need energy for chemical reactions to build larger molecules, as well as for movement and keeping warm.

items.stem: Which word equation represents aerobic respiration?

options.text: glucose + oxygen → lactic acid + water
carbon dioxide + water → glucose + oxygen
glucose + oxygen → ethanol + carbon dioxide
glucose + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water

items.why: This is the equation given in the specification for aerobic respiration: glucose and oxygen are used and carbon dioxide and water are produced.

items.stem: In the equation for aerobic respiration, what do the symbols C6H12O6 and H2O represent?

options.text: C6H12O6 is glucose and H2O is oxygen
C6H12O6 is oxygen gas and H2O is water
C6H12O6 is water and H2O is glucose
C6H12O6 is glucose and H2O is water

items.why: C6H12O6 is the symbol for glucose, the reactant, and H2O is the symbol for water, one of the products.

items.stem: How does the body react to the increased demand for energy during exercise?

options.text: the heart rate, breathing rate and breath volume rise
the breathing rate rises but the heart rate stays steady
the heart rate rises but the breath volume is steady
the breath volume rises but the heart rate is steady

items.why: The heart rate, breathing rate and breath volume increase during exercise to supply the muscles with more oxygenated blood.

items.stem: How is a lipid molecule formed in metabolism?

options.text: from three glycerols and one fatty acid
from a single glycerol and three amino acids
from three fatty acids and one glucose
from one glycerol and three fatty acids

items.why: Metabolism includes the formation of lipid molecules from a molecule of glycerol and three molecules of fatty acids.

items.stem: A muscle cell has no oxygen supply. Which substance builds up in the cell?

options.text: liquid ethanol, made from glucose
lactic acid, made from glucose
water vapour, made from glucose
carbon dioxide, made from glucose

items.why: Anaerobic respiration in muscles is represented by the equation glucose → lactic acid, so lactic acid builds up when insufficient oxygen is supplied.

items.stem: Why is much less energy transferred by anaerobic respiration than by aerobic respiration?

options.text: the oxidation of the glucose is faster
the glucose in cells is used up faster
the energy is used up making lactic acid
the oxidation of the glucose is incomplete

items.why: As the oxidation of glucose is incomplete in anaerobic respiration, much less energy is transferred than in aerobic respiration.

items.stem: Yeast is used in the manufacture of bread and alcoholic drinks. Which equation represents the respiration of the yeast in these processes?

options.text: glucose → lactic acid + carbon dioxide
glucose + oxygen → ethanol + water
glucose → ethanol + carbon dioxide
glucose + water → ethanol + oxygen

items.why: Anaerobic respiration in plant and yeast cells is represented by this equation. In yeast it is called fermentation: the carbon dioxide makes bread rise and the ethanol is in alcoholic drinks.

items.stem: A sprinter's muscles are not supplied with enough oxygen during a race. What happens in the muscles?

options.text: lactic acid builds up and an oxygen debt forms
carbon dioxide builds up and an oxygen debt forms
ethanol builds up and an oxygen debt is formed
lactic acid builds up and more energy is made

items.why: If insufficient oxygen is supplied, anaerobic respiration takes place in muscles; the incomplete oxidation of glucose causes a build up of lactic acid and creates an oxygen debt.

items.stem: After a race, what happens to the lactic acid that has built up in the muscles?

options.text: it is taken in the blood to the liver
it is broken down inside the muscles
it is breathed out through the lungs
it is turned to glucose in the blood

items.why: Blood flowing through the muscles transports the lactic acid to the liver where it is converted back into glucose.

items.stem: A plant cell synthesises protein. Which molecules does its metabolism use?

options.text: glucose and fatty acids, to make amino acids
glucose and nitrate ions, to make amino acids
glycerol and nitrate ions, to make amino acids
starch and nitrate ions, to make amino acids

items.why: Metabolism includes the use of glucose and nitrate ions to form amino acids which in turn are used to synthesise proteins.

items.stem: How does anaerobic respiration in muscle cells compare with aerobic respiration?

options.text: far more energy transferred, and lactic acid made
less energy transferred, and lactic acid made
less energy transferred, and ethanol made as well
less energy transferred, and carbon dioxide made

items.why: Anaerobic respiration in muscles is represented by glucose → lactic acid, and because the oxidation of glucose is incomplete much less energy is transferred than in aerobic respiration.
